opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new medicines — up 23% as the pipeline widened.

opex.name: Marketing, selling & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, advertising and running the company — up 30% to support new launches.

opex.name: Acquired IPR&D
opex.note: Research bought in from other companies, expensed on the spot.

footerNote: Reported (GAAP) figures throughout; Lilly's non-GAAP net income was $5.68B (EPS $6.31).
otherDetail: Net other expense of $91M — interest costs of $209M, partly offset by $118M of net other income.

segments.name: Mounjaro
segments.note: The diabetes and weight-loss shot — sales nearly doubled outside the U.S. as it entered new markets.

segments.name: Zepbound
segments.note: The weight-loss shot sold in the U.S. — sales nearly tripled on strong demand.

segments.name: All other medicines
segments.note: Everything else Lilly sells, including Verzenio at $1.5B.

takeaways.text: Mounjaro ($5.2B) and Zepbound ($3.4B) together brought in 55% of Lilly's revenue — Mounjaro grew 68% and Zepbound 172%.
takeaways.title: Two drugs are now most of the company

takeaways.text: Gross margin rose 3.5 points to 84.3% on better production costs and a richer product mix — so profit grew 91%, much faster than revenue.
takeaways.title: Margins widened

takeaways.text: After the strong first half, Lilly lifted its full-year 2025 revenue guidance to $60.0–62.0B.
takeaways.title: Guidance raised

verdict: Lilly's revenue jumped 38% to $15.6B as Mounjaro and Zepbound kept surging — and wider margins turned that growth into $5.7B of profit, up 91%.
